chunks: 3. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah, on the authority of Ahmad ibn Hilal, on the authority of al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fuddal, on the authority of Abu Hamzah, on the authority of Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: I heard him say:
There is nothing greater in reward than testifying that: 'There is no god but Allah,' because Allah, the Mighty and High, has nothing equal to Him, and no one shares His command.

key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god but Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the greatest act of worship in terms of reward according to the Imam?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the testimony of monotheism (Shahadah) as the most rewarding act, grounding its supremacy in Allah’s absolute uniqueness (Tawhid) where He is neither equaled nor partnered in His dominion. This highlights the Shia theological emphasis on *Tawhid al-Dhat* (Unity of Essence) as the foundational source of all spiritual merit, linking the verbal declaration directly to the metaphysical reality of God’s exclusive authority.
